# Not yet verified

The spec lists these as open; they are reported, never hidden:

- An omitted biorep is the line's 0-based index across all lines, the convention MetaMorpheus uses for a run with no design. It is the bridge's own default: mzLib has no reader that says what a run without a design is (MetaMorpheus's ExperimentalDesign reader lives in MetaMorpheus). If mzLib gains one, the bridge should use it and send nothing for an omitted field.
- Re-measure the K562 MBR pair at threads -1 on the current bridge (mzLib pin d10017ce; G-flashlfq-stale-caveats). Until then the caveat above states what mzLib\#1155 claims, not a bridge measurement. All three bindings already say so: \#1155 fixed it, it is not re-measured, and 1 is the conservative choice (pyMzLib since 0.3.0). When the re-measure passes, delete that sentence in all three.
- Default divergence: the wire, pyMzLib and mzLibRust default threads to -1; mzLibR defaults max\_threads to 1. R no longer warns on other values, and keeps 1 until the K562 re-measure above. Once that passes, pick one default for all three (G-flashlfq-stale-caveats).
- flashlfq\_small.json is hand-shaped (paths '/abs/...', 4 identifications), not recorded from a live bridge; a live recording would make the example executable against real files.
- ppm tolerances and mbr-q are not range-checked by the bridge (a negative or zero tolerance reaches FlashLFQ); the ranges above are FlashLFQ's meaningful ones, not enforced ones. An option given with no value is silently defaulted by the Arguments parser.
- A PSM file of an unsupported or non-quantifiable type crosses as correctness (mzLib's MzLibException from FileReader.ReadQuantifiableResultFile), though it is arguably the caller's mistake.
